From f75c9f110f0bc2cba401a8b95c9c4377c6c057e9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eran Mizrahi <eranmizra@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2011 21:10:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem introduced by commit 43e45eb94e1
which (wrongly) handled the 0xFEFF mark as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f72594567..54bb57f0a80 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `TextUtils.java`**
   - A single line of code was modified in the `TextUtils` class. The condition that checks for a range of Unicode characters was changed from:
     ```java
     (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)
     ```
     to:
     ```java
     (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)
     ```
   - This change effectively excludes the Unicode character 0xFEFF (the special Unicode marker) from being treated as part of the right-to-left (RTL) character range.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `TextUtils.java` directly addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (identified as commit `43e45eb94e1`). The bug involved incorrectly handling the Unicode marker 0xFEFF as an RTL character. By adjusting the upper limit of the character range check from 0xFEFF to 0xFEFE, the patch ensures that the 0xFEFF marker is no longer misclassified, thereby fixing the issue.

Here is the commit message:
RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem introduced by commit 43e45eb94e1
which (wrongly) handled the 0xFEFF mark as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the Unicode character 0xFEFF, which was mistakenly classified as part of the right-to-left (RTL) character range due to an inclusive range check in the code. This led to improper text rendering and behavior when the marker was present in the text.

Here is the patch:
 
     public static boolean isRTLCharacter(char c) {
         //range of RTL characters per unicode specification
         return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)
```
Reason:
This inclusive range check incorrectly classified the Unicode character 0xFEFF (the zero-width no-break space) as a right-to-left (RTL) character, leading to improper text rendering and behavior when this marker was present in the text.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
(c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)
```
Reason:
By changing the upper limit of the range from 0xFEFF to 0xFEFE, the code now correctly excludes the 0xFEFF character from being classified as an RTL character, thus resolving the rendering issue associated with this Unicode marker.
